text:
sam: Quick check — I'm seeing odd 429 behavior on the /v1/generate-batch endpoint after the recent burst-accounting change. Some clients get a Retry-After header, others get none. Anyone else?

toni: I saw that too in staging earlier. Might be related to the new per-customer soft-limit path we added. Did you repro with the same payload size?

sam: Yes, same payload. Two clients hit the same route within 200ms of each other; one got `Retry-After: 1`, other got a 429 with no header. Not consistent.

deepak: Can you paste the raw response bodies/headers? Could be the fallback path that returns a generic 429 without rate headers.

sam: Sure — copied from curl: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Quota-Bucket: cust-45-prod
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 1
{ "error": "rate_limited" }
```

and the other: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limited" }
```

irma: That second one looks like the generic global-fallback 429 we introduced for cold-starts/burst-shed. We intentionally skip headers there to avoid leaking exact quota tokens. But that was meant for edge nodes only.

toni: Right — the intent was: if request is dropped at edge for capacity reasons, return minimal 429. If dropped by quota engine, include the bucket + Retry-After. Looks like some quota rejections are being surfaced as edge drops due to timing.

sam: Feels bad for clients. Some SDKs retry only when Retry-After exists, others use exponential backoff on any 429. We're getting inconsistent client behavior.

deepak: Proposed fix: ensure quota engine always annotates with X-Quota-Bucket and at least a heuristic Retry-After when it decides to reject. Edge-only drops keep the minimal 429. That way clients can distinguish.

irma: That makes sense. Downside: leaking quota bucket IDs for some rejects. Is that a security concern?

deepak: The bucket id is internal but not user-secret; we already expose bucket tokens in other headers (for per-route dashboards). We can sanitize to `bucket:short-<hash>` if needed.

toni: Implementation notes: in runtime, the decision chain is: router -> admission control -> quota check -> accept/reject. The bug likely comes from a race where router times out waiting for quota check and triggers fallback error path (edge 429) while quota check later emits its own 429. We need to collapse to single source of truth and prefer quota's header when available.

sam: Action items: (1) add a small buffered handoff so router waits an extra 50ms for quota reply before doing fallback in low-latency configs; (2) make quota check always attach `X-Quota-Bucket` and `Retry-After` (even heuristic); (3) update SDK docs to recommend backoff on any 429 but honor Retry-After when present.

irma: Sounds good. I'll file a tiny RFC and PR for the header change. Deepak, can you look at the router timeout tweak? Might need perf signoff.

deepak: Yup — will prototype with a 50ms toleration window, run against perf harness. If latency regression <0.5% p95 we can go ahead.

quota-bot: Incident hint: spike in vhost "cust-45-prod" at 2024-06-11T18:23:40Z — several 429s emitted (see ops). Marking owner @deepak.

toni: Also FYI — embedding-batch clients do retries aggressively; we should ensure we don't create retry storms by returning Retry-After=0. Maybe floor Retry-After to 1s when we throttle bursts.

sam: Agreed, floor to 1s is safer. I'll include that in the RFC.

irma: Timeline: I'll open RFC today, sam/toni draft SDK note, deepak experiment tomorrow. Can we aim to have PRs by EOD Friday?

sam: That works for me. Thanks all :thumbsup:
